performance.text: The 7:40 bus was late again today. I stood at the stop for twenty minutes with my coffee getting cold. When it finally came it was packed, so I stood the whole way holding the pole next to a guy eating chips. I got to class right as the professor was taking attendance. She looked at me but didn't say anything. I think I'm going to start leaving at 7:15 even though I hate waking up that early. Or maybe I'll just bike when it gets warmer.

performance.text: I tried making my mom's lentil soup last night and it did not taste like hers. I used the same stuff, I think. Onions, garlic, cumin, red lentils, a lemon at the end. Mine came out kind of flat. I called her and she laughed and said I forgot to fry the spices first and also I probably didn't put enough salt. She was right about the salt. I'm going to try again on Sunday and actually write down what she says this time.

performance.text: Studied for the stats midterm at the library until it closed. I still don't really get confidence intervals. I can do the formula but if you ask me what it means I kind of freeze. My friend tried to explain it with a fishing net and that helped a little. The test is Thursday. I made flashcards but half of them are just me writing 'ask about this' on the back, which isn't great.

performance.text: Worked a double at the store on Saturday because Marcus called out. The morning was dead, maybe ten customers before noon. Then around three a whole youth soccer team came in for snacks and it was chaos. One kid tried to pay with a gift card from a different store. I was on my feet for eleven hours and my back still hurts. The manager bought everyone pizza at the end though, so that was nice.

performance.text: We lost 3-2 on Sunday and honestly we deserved it. Our first half was a mess. Nobody was talking, and twice I passed straight to the other team, which, great. Second half we woke up. Danny scored off a corner and I almost got one in the last minute but it hit the post. The sound of the ball hitting the post is the worst sound in the world. We play them again in three weeks.

performance.text: My phone fell out of my pocket on the stairs and the screen cracked into a spiderweb. It still works but I can't see the top left corner, which is where my email is, of course. The repair shop wanted ninety dollars. I'm not paying that right now. So I put a screen protector over the cracks and now it looks like the phone is wearing a bandage. My little sister thinks it's hilarious.

performance.text: Every summer we drove eight hours to my grandparents' house, and every summer my dad swore he'd leave earlier next year. He never did. I remember the back seat more than the trip itself: the cooler of sandwiches, my brother's elbow, the tape that only had one side that worked. My grandma would be on the porch before the car even stopped. She's been gone four years now. I still can't smell cardamom without thinking about that porch.

performance.text: Moving apartments is the worst. I thought I had maybe fifteen boxes of stuff. It was thirty-one. Where did all of it come from? I found three phone chargers that don't fit any phone I own and a birthday card from 2019 that I never opened. My friend helped me carry the couch up four flights and we had to take the legs off to get it around the corner. I owe him dinner. Probably several dinners.

performance.text: I spent two hours last night on a bug that turned out to be a missing comma. Two hours. I read the error message like ten times and it kept pointing at the wrong line, or at least I thought it was the wrong line. When I finally saw it I wasn't even happy, I was just tired. My roommate said that's how it goes and that it gets better. I hope he's right because I have another assignment due Friday.

performance.text: I've been building a little app to track my runs because the one I was using got a subscription. Right now it can show a list of runs and that's about it. The login part keeps breaking. I wanted to finish it before the spring 5K but that's in two weeks and I don't think that's happening. Still, the first time I saw my own list show up on my phone I kind of yelled.
